Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

cbr 0.1.0

Initial development version. R bindings to the controlledburn Rust crate for sparse scanline rasterization of polygons, lines, and points.

Crate

  • Built on controlledburn 0.2.0. The crate moved to 0-based indices, half-open run ranges (col_end exclusive) and id = k; cb_burn_wkb() converts at the boundary so R sees 1-based row/col, inclusive col_end and id/geom_index equal to the 1-based input position. Nothing changes for R code, and the cb_burn tables are identical to those from 0.1.0.

  • cb_burn_wkb() writes each output column straight into its R vector and frees the crate’s table as soon as its columns exist, and borrows the input WKB rather than copying it. Peak memory for a large burn is about twice the result size instead of three times.

  • Now built on controlledburn 0.3.1, from crates.io. Notable changes that reach R: multi-part geometries now get one record per cell (parts’ coverage is summed, and a cell the parts together fill becomes a run) instead of per-part records, so tables for multipolygons can differ from earlier builds, with the same total coverage; and rings too short to burn, and one-coordinate lines, now get a note instead of being skipped silently.

  • cb_burn(parity = TRUE) gives the C++ core’s records exactly (no run coalescing, per-part records for multi-part geometries).

  • cb_burn(threads = ) burns on several threads via the crate’s burn_par, with the same result as the serial burn. 0 uses all available threads; the default 1 is serial. Small burns stay serial regardless.

  • cb_burn(id_offset = ) adds a non-negative offset to every geometry id (and to geom_index in notes), recorded in attribute id_offset; n_geom stays the number of input geometries. cb_combine() joins burns of consecutive slices of a collection that share a grid (identical extent, dimension, crs and coverage) into the burn of the whole, record for record, whatever order they are given in. It refuses overlapping id ranges; a gap in the ids counts as empty geometries. summary(), plot() and cb_crop() respect the offset.

  • cb_burn_index() burns onto affine grids, rotated and sheared, given a GDAL geotransform and dimension. Geometry is moved into index space by the inverse of the geotransform and burned on a unit-cell lattice, so edge fractions are exact fractions of each cell’s own area, whatever its shape. The result is a cb_burn whose extent is the index lattice, with the world definition in attributes geotransform, world_extent and crs. cb_geotransform() builds a geotransform from an origin, cell size, rotation and shear. cb_cells() returns the cells as world-space polygons for plotting. cb_crop() moves an affine burn’s origin to the window, cb_combine() requires matching geotransforms, and cb_materialize() adds geotransform to the gis list (with bbox the world bounding box of the grid’s outline). lines$length is in world units on grids whose cells are similar to squares, and in cell units, with a warning, otherwise. See the “Rotated and sheared grids” vignette for a gallery.

  • New vignette, “Burning onto a model’s native ocean grid”: a polygon burned exactly onto the rectilinear part of the ACCESS-ESM1.6 ocean (MOM tripolar) grid in its native array order, with edges cut at the cell walls taken from the model’s corner coordinates, the 80°E seam handled by burning on two periods and folding, figures with ximage, and an area-weighted mean of temperature over a Southern Ocean sector. A 317 KB extract of the model’s grid and one temperature field ships in inst/extdata. Suggests ximage. The vignette also goes into the tripolar cap north of 65°N: cells as quadrilaterals in a polar stereographic plane, each split into four triangles mapped by area onto the unit cell (the exact curvilinear method of the crate’s design/grid-frontends.md), polygons cut at the triangles’ edges, and the grid’s fold handled by burning on a mirrored copy and folding back. An Arctic region around the pole burns exactly: its area to 1e-12, and each cell to 4e-8 against sf.

  • New article, “Cell predicates: exact all-touched and slivers”: the DE-9IM relations on Natural Earth countries at one degree. cbr’s exact all-touched (cb_materialize(value = "intersects")) against GDAL’s all-touched via terra::rasterize(touches = TRUE): 82 cells cbr finds that GDAL misses (borders on cell walls) and 4 GDAL burns that do not touch the country, all settled by GEOS. And the slivers the burn’s tolerance rounds away, with a check for invalid input: one of the crate book’s 18 slivers comes from Sudan’s self-intersecting polygon in Natural Earth. The countries ship in inst/extdata (public domain). Suggests terra.

  • The pkgdown site is built and deployed by GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml), with a hex logo drawn by cbr itself (data-raw/logo.R).

  • cb_relate() and cb_burn(relate = TRUE) (also cb_burn_index(relate = )) add a sixth table, relations: for each polygon, the DE-9IM intersection matrix (nine characters, e.g. "212F11FF2") against every cell whose closed box its boundary touches, including cells it only touches along a wall or at a corner, which have no record in the burn. Every other cell is "212FF1FF2" if it is in the polygon’s runs and "FF2FF1212" otherwise. The matrices come from the geometry, not the burn’s records, so they see the slivers the burn’s 1e-6 coverage tolerance rounds away. Computed by the crate’s relate_cells (controlledburn 0.3.1); matrices match sf::st_relate cell by cell in the tests, including on rotated and sheared grids. cb_crop() crops the table with the others and cb_combine() binds it (all burns or none). cb_relate() needs the geometry again, since a burn does not keep it, and refuses cropped burns.

  • Spatial predicates per cell, from a burn’s runs and relations: cb_matrix() looks up the DE-9IM matrix of any cell (relations where the boundary touches, otherwise covered for run cells and disjoint for the rest; NA off the grid and for lines and points). cb_cells_where() selects cells by predicate ("intersects", "interiors_meet", "covers", "touches", "covered_by") or by DE-9IM pattern. cb_materialize() gains those predicates as values, counting the polygons satisfying each per cell; value = "intersects" is the exact all-touched mask, including wall and corner contacts and the slivers the burn rounds away. cb_slivers() lists the cells where the burn’s records and the exact topology disagree. Tested against GEOS (sf::st_relate and its named predicates) on every cell; on Natural Earth countries at one degree it reproduces the crate’s figures (12 interior and 6 exterior slivers, 78 touching cells).

Burning

  • cb_burn() rasterizes any geometry that wk::as_wkb() understands onto a regular grid given extent = c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax) and dimension = c(ncol, nrow). The result is a cb_burn object: five data frames (runs, edges, lines, points, notes) with the grid stored in attributes. Indices are 1-based and row 1 is the top row; geometry k gets id = k.

  • extent defaults to the bounding box of geom (wk::wk_bbox(), reordered to c(xmin, xmax, ymin, ymax)), and dimension defaults to 256 columns with the number of rows computed so that cells are square in the units of extent. A single dimension value is taken as ncol.

  • coverage = TRUE (default) returns polygon interiors as horizontal runs of fully covered cells and boundary cells with their exact coverage fraction in edges. coverage = FALSE uses the faster cell-centre (fasterize-style) rule and emits runs only.

  • cb_burn_wkb() is the low-level worker taking a list of raw WKB blobs and the grid parameters directly.

  • Non-fatal per-geometry problems (for example unclosed rings, which are closed silently) are reported in the notes table rather than raised as errors.

Cropping and materializing

  • cb_crop() snaps an extent to the cell boundaries of a burn grid (snap = "out", "in", or "near") and subsets the tables to that window. No geometry is re-rasterized: runs that straddle the window edge are clipped and all indices are re-based, so the result is a valid cb_burn on the smaller grid. The parent grid and the window’s c(col, row) offset within it are recorded in the parent attribute.

  • cb_materialize() expands a burn into a dense cell vector in the layout of gdalraster::read_ds(): one element per cell, row-major from the top-left, with a gis attribute (type, bbox, dim, srs, datatype). This format is produced without any dependency on gdalraster. value selects the cell contents: "coverage" (summed coverage, Float32), "id" (highest geometry id wins, Int32), or "count" (distinct geometries per cell, Int32). Untouched cells take background (default NA).

  • cb_as_matrix() reshapes a materialized vector (from cb_materialize() or gdalraster::read_ds()) into an nrow x ncol matrix oriented as on a map.

Summarizing and plotting

  • summary() for cb_burn describes a burn in time proportional to the number of records, never to the number of cells: exact per-row and per-column covered-cell marginals (the column marginal via a difference array over run endpoints), the content extent of touched cells, per-geometry area (interior cells, summed boundary fractions, line length, point count), edge-fraction quantiles, and a coarse overview raster. print() reports these, with ascii = TRUE for a text rendering of the overview.

  • cb_overview() aggregates a burn onto square tiles of block cells and returns mean coverage per tile in the read_ds layout, so it is the same shape as cb_materialize() and equal to it when block = 1. Runs spanning several tiles are handled with a difference array along the tile row, so the cost is records plus tiles regardless of block size.

  • plot() for cb_burn draws the grid extent with asp = 1 and either every record as a rectangle (what = "exact": runs, edge cells shaded by fraction, optionally coloured by_id) or the overview raster (what = "overview"), switching automatically on a record-count threshold. Marginal strips along the top and right show the exact column and row totals even when the main panel is an overview.

  • plot(what = "exact") on small grids (no side longer than detail, default 64 cells) also shows the record structure: a thin white line through the cells of each run, and each edge cell numbered by its position in the edges table, so the records can be counted off the picture.

  • cb_crop() with no extent crops to the content extent.

  • cb_burn() records the number of input geometries in attribute n_geom.

  • print() for cb_burn summarizes the grid, mode, table sizes, and (for a cropped burn) the offset within the parent grid.
